subtype: Approach: setting a time limit for deciding [Action]
passage: I'm Indu. Last week our group could not choose a topic for our project, and we had been going in circles since Monday. Ishita said the sports day would be good, and Nikhil wanted space. I looked at the clock and had an idea. "Let's give ourselves five minutes. If we can't decide by then, we toss a coin." Everybody agreed, and Nikhil set the timer on his watch. We each said our reasons quickly. Sports won by two votes, and we did not even need the coin. We started drawing before the bell rang, and I felt relieved. It was simple, but it worked.

qa.q: How long did Indu suggest for choosing the topic?
What was Indu feeling before making the suggestion?
qa.a: Indu was probably impatient and worried about wasted time, since the group had been going in circles since Monday.

qa.q: What alternative approach could the group use, and why?
qa.a: They could list all the ideas and vote, or let the teacher choose. Either would end the circling and let them start on the actual project.

qa.q: How might Nikhil have seen the time limit?
qa.a: Nikhil was willing to set the timer, so the limit probably felt fair and useful to Nikhil, who wanted a different topic but accepted the vote.

grounding: A girl proposes a five-minute limit with a coin toss as backup, and the limit stops the endless talk so the group can start.
